'''Jean-Michel Raimond''' (born {{birth date|1955|12|11|df=y}} in [[Orléans]]<ref name="cv">{{cite web|url= http://www.cqed.org/spip.php?article335?lang=en|title=Curriculum vitae|website=cqed.org|access-date=1 August 2015}}</ref>) is a French [[physicist]] working in the field of [[quantum mechanics]].

== Biography ==
Raimond enrolled at the [[École normale supérieure (rue d'Ulm)]] (ENS) in 1975. After graduating with a DEA  in atomic and molecular physics, his first research work was in [[superradiance]] and [[Rydberg atoms]].

He became Research Associate and Research Fellow at the [[Centre national de la recherche scientifique]] (CNRS), working under [[Serge Haroche]] towards his 1984 thesis {{lang|fr|Propriétés radiatives des atomes de Rydberg dans une cavité résonnante}} ("Radiative properties of Rydberg atoms in a resonant cavity").<ref>{{cite web|url=http://tel.archives-ouvertes.fr/docs/00/06/10/98/PDF/1984RAIMOND.pdf |language=fr |title=Propriétés radiatives des atomes de Rydberg dans une cavité résonnante|trans-title=Radiative properties of Rydberg atoms in a resonant cavity |first=Jean-Michel |last=Raimond |publisher=tel.archives-ouvertes.fr |access-date=25 June 2015}}</ref>

Since 1988, he has taught at the [[Université Pierre-et-Marie-Curie]].

From 1994 to 1999, he was a junior member of the [[Institut universitaire de France]].

From 2001 to 2011, he was a senior member and held the chair of [[quantum optics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://iuf.amue.fr/author/jraimond/ |title=Jean-Michel RAIMOND |publisher=IUF.amue.fr |access-date=25 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150623123607/http://iuf.amue.fr/author/jraimond/ |archive-date=23 June 2015 }}</ref>

From 2004 to 2009, he was head of the Department of Physics at the [[École normale supérieure (rue d'Ulm)]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.phys.ens.fr/spip.php?article130 |access-date=23 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130401131359/http://www.phys.ens.fr/spip.php?article130 |archive-date=1 April 2013 |title=Département de Physique de l'Ecole Normale supérieure - Histoire brève }}</ref>

Raimond specialised in [[atomic physics]] and [[quantum optics]] as a member of the [[Kastler-Brossel Laboratory]] in the {{lang|fr|Groupe d'Électrodynamique Quantique en Cavité}}, which he ran with the 2012 [[Nobel Prize]] winner [[Serge Haroche]]<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.leparisien.fr/sciences/nobel-de-physique-un-francais-et-un-americain-se-partagent-le-prix-09-10-2012-2218483.php|title=Nobel de Physique: un Français et un Américain se partagent le prix|language=fr|trans-title=Nobel Prize for Physics: A Frenchman and an American share the prize|newspaper=[[Le Parisien]]|date=9 October 2012}}</ref> and [[Michel Brune]].

He became interested in [[Rydberg atoms]], because their relatively large size and sensitivity to [[microwave radiation]] makes them particularly suited to studies of [[matter/energy interaction]]. He demonstrated that these atoms, coupled to superconducting cavities containing some [[photon]]s, are ideal systems for testing the laws of [[quantum decoherence]] and for demonstrating the possibility of constructing the components of [[quantum logic]], with promising results for their use in [[informatics]].<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Rev. Mod. Phys. |issue=73, 565 |title=Manipulating quantum entanglement with atoms and photons in a cavity |date=28 August 2001 |doi=10.1103/revmodphys.73.565 |volume=73 |pages=565–582 |last1=Raimond |first1=J. M. |last2=Brune |first2=M. |last3=Haroche |first3=S. |bibcode=2001RvMP...73..565R }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|arxiv=quant-ph/0105062|title=Controlled entanglement of two field modes in a Cavity Quantum Electrodynamics experiment |journal=Physical Review A |volume=64 |issue=5 |article-number=050301 |date=14 May 2001 |last1= Rauschenbeutel |first1=A. |last2= Bertet |first2=P. |last3= Osnaghi |first3=S. |last4= Nogues |first4=G. |last5= Brune |first5=M. |last6= Raimond |first6=J. M. |last7= Haroche |first7=S. |doi=10.1103/PhysRevA.64.050301 |bibcode=2001PhRvA..64e0301R |s2cid=1842697 }}</ref>

His most recent work, quoted in the 2012 Nobel Prize-winning work,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/laureates/2012/ |title=The Nobel Prize in Physics 2012 |publisher=Nobelprize.org |date=2012 |access-date=25 June 2015}}</ref> allows photons to be counted in the cavity without their being destroyed, thus directly demonstrating the quantum [[measurement problem]].<ref>{{Cite journal|arxiv=quant-ph/0612031|title=Quantum jumps of light recording the birth and death of a photon in a cavity |journal=Nature |volume=446 |issue=7133 |pages=297–300 |last1=Gleyzes |first1=Sébastien |last2=Kuhr |first2=Stefan |last3=Guerlin |first3=Christine |last4=Bernu |first4=Julien |last5=Deléglise |first5=Samuel |author6=Ulrich Busk Hoff |last7=Brune journal|arxiv=0707.3880|title=Progressive field-state collapse and quantum non-demolition photon counting |journal=Nature |volume=448 |issue=7156 |pages=889–93 |date=26 July 2007 |last1=Guerlin |first1=Christine |last2=Bernu |first2=Julien |last3=Deléglise |first3=Samuel |last4=Sayrin |first4=Clément |last5=Gleyzes |first5=Sébastien |last6=Kuhr |first6=Stefan |last7=Brune |first7=Michel |last8=Raimond |first8=Jean-Michel |last9=Haroche |first9=Serge |doi=10.1038/nature06057 |pmid=17713527|bibcode=2007Natur.448..889G |s2cid=4429859 }}</ref> This ideal measure also helps combat [[quantum decoherence]] with a [[quantum feedback]] scheme which keeps the number of photons in the cavity constant.<ref>{{Cite journal|arxiv=1107.4027|title=Real-time quantum feedback prepares and stabilizes photon number states |journal=Nature |volume=477 |issue=7362 |pages=73–77 |date=20 July 2011|last1=Sayrin |first1=Clément |last2=Dotsenko |first2=Igor |last3=Zhou |first3=Xingxing |last4=Peaudecerf |first4=Bruno |last5=Rybarczyk |first5=Théo |last6=Gleyzes |first6=Sébastien |last7=Rouchon |first7=Pierre |last8=Mirrahimi |first8=Mazyar |last9=Amini |first9=Hadis |last10=Brune |first10=Michel |last11=Raimond |first11=Jean-Michel |last12=Haroche |first12=Serge |doi=10.1038/nature10376 |pmid=21886159|bibcode=2011Natur.477...73S |s2cid=4383517 }}</ref>

Raimond is the son of [[Michel Raimond]], late professor of [[French literature]] at the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.babelio.com/auteur/Michel-Raimond/31966 |title=Michel Raimond (auteur de Le roman) |publisher=Babelio.com  |language=fr |date= |access-date=25 June 2015}}</ref>

==Awards==
* Prix Fernand Holweck by the [[Académie des sciences (France)|Académie des sciences]] (1985)
* Grand [[prix Ampère de l'Électricité de France]], given by the [[Académie des sciences (France)|Académie des sciences]], with M. Brune (1998)
* Grand [[Prix Jean-Ricard]] by the [[Société française de physique]] (2007)
* Gay-Lussac-Humboldt research award by the [[Fondation Alexander von Humboldt]] (2012)
* European Physical Society Edison-Volta prize (2014)<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.epsnews.eu/2014/02/raimond-eps-ed-volta-prize/ | title=Jean-Michel Raimond wins EPS Edison-Volta Prize 2014 &#124; e-EPS}}</ref>
* [[Chevalier de la Légion d'honneur]]
* Officer of the [[Ordre des Palmes Académiques]]

Lett.|issue=24|pages=4887–4890|year=1996|doi=10.1103/physrevlett.77.4887|pmid=10062660|volume=77|bibcode=1996PhRvL..77.4887B|doi-access=free}} In this experiment, for the first time, [[wave function collapse]] was observed using quantum mechanical methods.
*{{cite journal|first1=J. M.|last1=Raimond|first2=M|last2=Brune|first3=S.|last3=Haroche|author3-link=Serge Haroche|title=Manipulating quantum entanglement with atoms and photons in a cavity|journal=Rev. Mod. Phys.|issue=3|pages=565–582|year=2001|doi=10.1103/revmodphys.73.565|volume=73|bibcode=2001RvMP...73..565R}}). Peer reviewed article describing in particular quantum logical operations.
* {{cite book|first1=S.|last1=Haroche|first2=J. M.|last2=Raimond|title=Exploring the Quantum: Atoms, Cavities, and photons|publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]|place=Oxford|date=10 August 2006}}
* {{cite journal|first1=S.|last1=Gleyzes|title=Quantum jumps of light recording the birth and death of a photon in a cavity|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|place=London|issue=7133|pages=297–300|year=2007|display-authors=etal|doi=10.1038/nature05589|volume=446|pmid=17361178|bibcode=2007Natur.446..297G|arxiv=quant-ph/0612031|s2cid=4428931}} First ideal measurement (i.e. without quantum demolition) of the number of photons in a cavity.
* {{cite journal|first=C.|last=Guerlin|title=Progressive field state collapse and quantum non demolition photon counting|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|place=London|issue=7156|pages=889–893|year=2007|display-authors=etal|doi=10.1038/nature06057|volume=448|pmid=17713527|bibcode=2007Natur.448..889G|arxiv=0707.3880|s2cid=4429859}}
* {{cite journal|first=C.|last=Sayri|title=Real time quantum feedback prepares and stabilizes photon number states|journal=[[Nature (journal)|Nature]]|place=London|issue=7362|pages=73–77|date=2011|display-authors=etal|doi=10.1038/nature10376|volume=477|pmid=21886159|bibcode=2011Natur.477...73S|arxiv=1107.4027|s2cid=4383517}} First demonstration of a quantum retroaction schema in a quantum continuum.
